regime_context: The detector shows a defensive, healthcare-heavy leadership structure: Big Pharma leads the eligible trend-gated set (rank 2, score 1.245), with Health Care EW, Defensives, and Consumer Staples EW all high in the rank but also crowded (z-tested 1.3–1.7). The absolute-trend gate is validated for this market (gate_helps true), so leaning toward confirmed trend-eligible names with high durability is the only detector leg that warrants modest weight. The rotation margin between leader Memory/HBM (ineligible) and Big Pharma is razor-thin and the detector's own backtest labels rotation timing 'display only', so no handoff call is justified.
emerging_watch: Watch whether Memory, HBM & Storage (currently rank 1 but ineligible, durability_bar 0.35) regains trend-gate eligibility while Big Pharma's durability_bar holds above ~0.65. If Memory becomes eligible AND Big Pharma's breadth drops below ~0.5 while the rotation margin widens beyond the current 0.075, the defensive-to-semiconductor handoff would be worth renaming as CONFIRMED — until then it remains a display-only rotation signal with no forward weight.

theses.subject: Big Pharma
theses.thesis: Big Pharma is the highest-scoring eligible theme that also passes the absolute-trend gate (eligible true, durability_bar 0.78), which is the single validated drawdown-control leg in this market. Its trend health is strong (hurst_tag trend, breadth 0.889) and it is the current headline narrative, supported by a defensive macro backdrop with high unscheduled-surprise share. This is not a momentum buy into a rank — it is a read that the confirmed defensive leadership deserves to remain a directional lean while the trend gate holds.
evidence: eligible true and headline id equals big_pharma
durability_bar 0.78 (highest among top-ranked eligible healthcare names)
backtest verdict: absolute_trend_gate is the one validated risk-control leg and gate_helps true
theses.dissent: Big Pharma is crowded (crowding_z 1.33, crowded true) and its rank is only #2 — the ineligible Memory/HBM theme outranks it on raw score, so if that leadership window reopens the relative support for Pharma could fade. Healthcare also has multiple overlapping proxies (XLV, PPH) making the theme internally redundant.

falsifier.text: PPH lags the S&P 500 by 5% or more over any rolling 10-day stretch within the next 20 trading days

theses.subject: Health Care (Equal-Weight)
theses.thesis: This equal-weight healthcare sleeve passes the trend gate (durability_bar 0.73) with high breadth (0.817) and trend health. It captures the defensive rotation without single-stock concentration, which mitigates the crowding concern of the Pharma-specific basket. Momentum rank alone is a focus lens, but the trend-gate eligibility plus durability supports a modest directional lean.
theses.dissent: Crowded at z 1.46 (the highest in the top cohort after staples), and healthcare leadership is already broad — if the defensive trade unwinds, equal-weight health has no idiosyncratic buffer versus the cap-weighted Pharma tilt.

falsifier.text: XLV underperforms XLP by 8% or more over the next 20 trading days

theses.subject: Consumer Staples (Equal-Weight)
theses.thesis: Staples is trend-eligible (durability_bar 0.81) with strong durability and breadth (0.818). In a high-unscheduled-surprise macro backdrop with defensive leadership across healthcare and utilities, staples is a coherent, vol-aware extension of the same confirmed narrative — not a prediction of a new one. The trend gate provides the modesty discipline.
evidence: rank 6 overall with crowded_z 1.69 as size-down caution only
theses.dissent: Extremely crowded (z 1.69), and the same low-growth defensive tilt is already expressed in Defensives and Utilities — crowding here is a cap, not a buy, and staples is the most consensus-crowded of the defensive pack.

falsifier.text: XLP gives up 60% of its trailing 20-day advance relative to the S&P 500 within the next 20 trading days

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
